us_regulations: UL 62368-1 (safety – voluntary but often required by retailers)
common_pitfalls: EMC failures on conducted emissions – add filtering early
LVD requires testing to the specific product standard, not just 62368-1
WEEE registration required per country – often missed for first-time exporters

usb_powered_device.note: LVD (2014/35/EU) typically does NOT apply – USB PD max 20V DC is below the 75V DC threshold. However, EMC still applies.
en_standards: EN 62368-1 (Safety – may apply depending on product function)
common_pitfalls: USB PD negotiation failures can cause overcurrent – test all PD profiles
Even though LVD may not apply, safety testing is still expected by retailers
CE marking still required (EMC + RoHS)

battery_powered_device.description: Devices with integrated or removable batteries
us_regulations: DOT/IATA regulations for shipping lithium batteries
common_pitfalls: UN 38.3 transport testing is mandatory – cannot ship lithium batteries without it
Battery Regulation 2023/1542 requires removable batteries from 2027
Thermal runaway risk – include protection circuits (BMS)
WEEE + battery take-back obligations are separate registrations

iot_device.description: Connected devices with WiFi, BLE, or cellular
iot_device.note: RED (2014/53/EU) replaces both LVD and EMC for radio equipment – single directive covers safety, EMC, and spectrum.
en_standards: ETSI EN 303 645 (Cybersecurity for IoT – becoming mandatory)
us_regulations: FCC Part 15 (intentional radiator – requires FCC ID)
FCC Part 15 Subpart C or E depending on technology
common_pitfalls: RED requires Notified Body if no harmonised standard covers your radio tech
FCC intentional radiator requires FCC ID (not just supplier DoC)
Cybersecurity requirements (ETSI EN 303 645) becoming mandatory in EU from 2025
OTA updates must not break compliance

wireless_device.description: Devices with radio transmitters (WiFi, BLE, cellular, LoRa, Zigbee, NFC)
us_regulations: FCC Part 15 (intentional radiator – FCC ID required)
common_pitfalls: Each radio technology may need separate testing
Antenna design affects compliance – changes require re-testing
Module exemption possible if using pre-certified radio module

kitchen_appliance.description: Electrical kitchen and food preparation appliances
common_pitfalls: Food contact materials must comply with EC 1935/2004 – migration testing required
Part 2 of EN 60335 is product-specific – you must find the right one
Thermal fuse and safety cutout requirements are strict

heating_device.description: Electric heating products (heaters, heated garments, mug warmers)
common_pitfalls: Fire risk is #1 recall reason for heating products – thermal fuse mandatory
Overheat protection must be independent of main control
Surface temperature limits (EN 60335-1 Clause 11)
25%+ of CPSC heating device recalls cite fire/burn hazard

food_contact_product.description: Products that contact food (utensils, containers, packaging)
food_contact_product.note: If also electrical, add LVD + EMC + RoHS + WEEE directives.
common_pitfalls: Migration testing conditions depend on food type and temperature
Silicone, stainless steel, and ceramics each have specific test protocols
Printing inks and adhesives on food packaging also require compliance

lighting.description: LED lights, lamps, luminaires, and lighting fixtures
common_pitfalls: Blue light hazard assessment (EN 62471) often overlooked
Flicker requirements tightening – check IEC/TR 61547-1
Ecodesign requirements (EU 2019/2020) set minimum efficiency
Efficiency standards (ErP/DoE) are mandatory – minimum efficiency levels
Creepage and clearance distances critical for safety
No-load power consumption limits

wearable.description: Wearable electronics (smartwatches, fitness trackers, smart rings)
us_regulations: FCC SAR testing (if worn on body)
common_pitfalls: SAR testing required for devices worn on the body
Skin contact materials need biocompatibility assessment
Battery removability requirements (EU Battery Reg 2027)
Water resistance claims need IP rating testing

toy.description: Products designed for play by children under 14
us_regulations: ASTM F963 (Standard Consumer Safety Specification for Toy Safety)
common_pitfalls: Small parts testing mandatory for children under 3
Chemical testing is expensive and must cover many substances
Notified Body assessment required for chemical and electrical safety in EU
CPSIA requires third-party testing and Children's Product Certificate

medical_device_class_I.note: Medical Device Regulation (MDR) replaces most other directives for medical devices. This is a complex regulatory area – consider professional regulatory affairs support.
us_regulations: FDA 510(k) or De Novo (depending on classification)
common_pitfalls: MDR is significantly stricter than the old MDD – transition is ongoing
Even Class I devices need technical documentation and EU DoC
UDI (Unique Device Identification) now required in EUDAMED
Software as Medical Device (SaMD) has its own classification rules

us_regulations: CPSC tip-over standards (ASTM F2057 for dressers)
common_pitfalls: Tip-over risk is the #1 cause of furniture recalls
REACH applies to finishes, adhesives, and foam
No CE marking required for non-electrical furniture, but GPSD applies
Flammability testing required for most textiles
AZO dyes restricted under REACH Annex XVII
CPSIA applies to all children's textile products

packaging.description: Product packaging (standalone, not as part of another product)
common_pitfalls: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) registration required in most EU states
Heavy metal limits in packaging materials
France, Germany, Italy have strict packaging registration requirements
